source: CARDI Farmer Notes variety leaflets (KA15, Phka Romdoul, KA4, KA14, IR66, Sen Kraob 01); Climate Resilient Broadcasting Rice Growing Technique, ASPIRE/IFAD, MAFF, 2018
text:
Harvest when the grain is fully mature rather than by the calendar alone: the right moment is when more than half of the upper part of the panicle has turned deep golden-ripe and the lower half of the panicle is pale golden, with the panicle's neck (base) showing a dark straw-brown color. A practical field check smallholders use: roughly 30 days after the rice has finished flowering, once 80-85% of grains have taken on a husk-golden color and grain below the awn has hardened past the soft milky stage, the crop is ready to cut -- grain that still feels soft or milky when pinched needs more time.

After cutting, thresh as soon as practically possible; delaying threshing after cutting increases shattering losses and lets weather damage set in. Separate out diseased, discolored, or broken grain from the main harvest immediately at threshing rather than mixing it in, since it lowers the value of the whole batch if left mixed.
